speaker: shelleybrindle
text: So good evening and thanks for joining us virtually tonight. Just a reminder, public comment will only be accepted via Zoom, although we are live streaming for viewing only on Facebook. And the replay will always be available on Facebook, YouTube and TV 36. Just a quick update on COVID cases. As Jim mentioned, it's not a very promising trajectory at all. Today, there were 4,383 new cases in New Jersey, another 711 still under investigation and 313,863 total cases to date. Union County reported 26,752 and Westfield reported 18 new cases since my last update on Friday, three on Saturday, five on Sunday, two on Monday and eight today. I do expect these numbers to increase significantly when we get updated health department data, which includes rapid tests. And usually we get it on Friday, but due to the holiday, I'm not sure. But as we've seen in the last few weeks, I expect that number of 18 to go up significantly. Just a few updates in case you haven't heard from the governor's office, small businesses are eligible for discounts on PPE. We are also working aggressively with them and the state on anticipation of a vaccine. And so I know Megan from the health department, they're all working on what the equitable distribution of that will be. And the goal is vaccinating 70% of the adult population in six months. And lastly, I'd just say, there's the Union County Board of Commission's just announced a new rest easy caregivers grant, which provides opportunities for families in need of assistance in caring for children with disabilities and special needs during COVID. So I think there's approximately $1 million of federal CARES Act dollars are gonna be allocated to this program. So please, if you find yourself in a situation where you're caring for children with special needs, please reach out if you have any questions so we can help you facilitate that application. Moving on to local things, just wanna ask if you or anyone you know is interested in opening up a restaurant or bar in our north side train station, we provide the liquor license at no cost to the applicant, except for the $2,000 a year application fee. We just sent out a revised request for proposal, which has recently been posted on our website, which now includes blueprints, which we didn't have before, courtesy of Greg Redington from Redcom Design. So the deadline for submissions is January 12th. And if anyone is interested, I would encourage them to pick up an application. I think there's a walkthrough at the station on December 4th. And speaking of transit, last week I attended a meeting with New Jersey Transit Executives to represent the Raritan Valley Line Mayor's Alliance, along with members of the Raritan Valley Rail Coalition. And we are working together to advocate for the expansion of one seat ride service along the Raritan Valley Line. In light of the potential long-term COVID impact on overall ridership, we believe that now is the right time to reassess and equitably allocate one seat rides. New Jersey Transit committed to providing potential options for some shoulder peak service, and we're gonna have a discussion in February. They are totally focused on the positive train control obligations, which they have to be met by year-end. Lifelong Westfield Team is inviting seniors to a Zoom webinar with Chief Battelora on December 9th at 11 o'clock to discuss scams that target the senior population, how to avoid them, especially during the holiday season. So if you are a senior or no one, please encourage them to attend. And thank you, Chief Battelora, for that. I invite everybody in the public to join me next Thursday, December 3rd at noon for a Facebook Live that I'll be hosting with Town Planner Don Samet, Phil Abramson from our redevelopment firm Topology, and Richard Heaps from StreetWorks who presented at the last council meeting about their approach to smart redevelopment as they consider the future of their Lord and Taylor property. Our panel discussion will address how other communities have handled notable inflection points and transformations, the power of community input, and the potential impact of COVID on Westfield's future as we analyze how to best position the town for success. So I think it's a great opportunity to hear from the experts on what they're seeing nationally, statewide, and opportunities that we should be considering in town for what I like to say, for Westfield to become a premier post-COVID community. On another note, today we announced that we are kicking off the holiday season with a significant town-wide initiative called Be the Light. It's to raise awareness and funds for hunger and food insecurity here in Union County. We're extremely fortunate to have Goo Goo Dolls front man and Westfield resident John Resnick willing to use his large platform to promote this event. It was an idea he initiated after he successfully kicked off our fundraiser for We Love Local in the spring. We will be doing a live stream performance on the town's Facebook page Sunday night at six o'clock, which will be followed by an online auction for donated items such as a personal backyard performance from John himself, a signed guitar, and autographed copies of the Goo Goo Dolls' new Christmas album. Donations will be made to the Westfield United Fund with proceeds going to the Westfield Food Pantry and the Community Food Bank of New Jersey. I can't think of a better way to celebrate the spirit of the season. You can find out all the details on our website. And the holidays is here, obviously, and it will look different this year in many respects, but people have been very hard at work to make sure that there's still plenty of cheer to enjoy in town. Our annual tree lighting and menorah lighting will still be taking place, albeit virtually, due to the restrictions on outdoor gatherings. And I've asked DWC liaison counsel, Don Mackey, to provide an update later on many of the planned activities in store, including a gingerbread contest, a holiday light contest, free parking, gift wrapping, and more. I just would simply like to reiterate how much our businesses need your support over these critical weeks ahead, which will make or break many of them. And I presume your Thanksgiving gathering will be smaller than usual this year, much like mine is gonna be. It's just one more sacrifice we all must continue to make to keep everyone safe, especially as COVID cases continue to surge. But there is light at the end of the tunnel with the recent positive developments surrounding vaccines, which should give us all hope. We just have to stay vigilant until we get there. So please, please, especially over the holidays, I know our public health officials are very, very worried about potential outbreaks resulting from Thanksgiving. So just do your part and maintain, you know, small gatherings and just be safe. And lastly, I'm sorry to conclude these remarks on a very sad note. Last night, a longtime Westfield resident and planning board chairman, Robert Newell, passed away after a courageous battle with cancer. Robert's dedication to this community knew no bounds, and I am grateful for the opportunity I had to get to know him. I had the benefit of his warm embrace when I was a new member of the planning board and he patiently taught me the ropes. As a longtime Westfielder, he surprised me with his openness to new ideas, which only seemed to energize him. He was the consummate volunteer, a gentleman's gentleman, and man who lived his life with honor and grace. I would ask if you'll just join me in a moment of silence in honor of Robert Newell. Thank you. We'll now move on to tonight's agenda. So Tara, do we have any advertised hearings?
